key: Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy: therein let them rejoice. It is better than what they hoard.
s: Just after an exhortation and a balm for the breasts is announced to mankind, the Prophet is told what to say; al-Tabari, on 10:58, reads the bounty as Islam and the mercy as the Qur’an, each worth more than this world’s wealth and treasure.

evidence.words: ﴿بفضل الله﴾ ، أيها الناس، الذي تفضل به عليكم، وهو الإسلام، فبيَّنه لكم، ودعاكم إليه = ﴿وبرحمته﴾ ، التي رحمكم بها، فأنزلها إليكم، فعلَّمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون من كتابه، وبصَّركم بها معالم دينكم، وذلك القرآن = ﴿فبذلك فليفرحوا هو خير مما يجمعون﴾ ، يقول: فإن الإسلام الذي دعاهم إليه، والقرآن الذي أنزله عليهم، خيرٌ مما يجمعون من حُطَام الدنيا وأموالها وكنوزها
evidence.gloss: “In the bounty of God”, O people, with which He has favoured you: that is Islam, which He made plain to you and called you to; “and in His mercy”, with which He had mercy on you and sent down to you, teaching you from His Book what you did not know: that is the Qur’an. “Therein let them rejoice; it is better than what they hoard”: the Islam He called them to and the Qur’an He sent down are better than the debris of this world, its wealth and its treasures, that they amass.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Yunus 10:58, at 1421; two whole sentences). Plain sense faithful: 10:57 addresses mankind with an exhortation, a balm for what is in the breasts, a guidance and a mercy, and 10:58 opens with “Say”; no four-word run from the key. I read al-Tabari’s whole comment on 10:58: his own gloss (Abu Ja’far) makes the bounty Islam and the mercy the Qur’an, both better than this world’s debris, wealth and treasures; he then gives the agreeing reports, a minority reversing the pair (bounty the Qur’an, mercy Islam), and his preference for the ya reading, taking the ayah as said of the polytheists. The sentence paraphrases his own gloss; “each worth more” fairly distributes his joint “Islam and the Qur’an are better than what they amass”. 44 words; entry-check ok.
